subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core enforced execution-progress contract for artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and post-green follow-through, or keep this limited to existing loop/stale-run guardrails plus narrower bug fixes?
rationale: The missing mechanism is real, but the requested solution defines durable state ownership, config/flag behavior, channel-visible enforcement, timers, telemetry, and false-positive policy that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require an MVP that uses existing runner/diagnostic events, SQLite state, telemetry, and default-off or measured rollout before enforcement.

options.title: Split into narrower bug fixes
options.body: Track only concrete live reproductions against tool loops, stale-run recovery, timeout diagnostics, and outbound fake-progress gates while deferring a unified enforcement contract.

options.title: Decline broad enforcement
options.body: Close the broad direction as too policy-heavy for core and rely on current loop detection, liveness diagnostics, and operator monitoring.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require an MVP that uses existing runner/diagnostic events, SQLite state, telemetry, and default-off or measured rollout before enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-history owner for the central runtime guardrail files and the prior configurable loop-detection change.
